# Cambiaro

> A currency converter for people and AI agents. Converts between 165 world
> currencies using live and historical European Central Bank reference rates,
> installs as an offline-capable Progressive Web App, and exposes every action
> as a typed WebMCP tool that an AI agent can call directly.

Site: https://cambiaro.programmersingh.dev/
Cost: free. No account or API key is required.
Source: https://github.com/theprogrammersingh/cambiaro

## What it does

- Converts an amount between any two of 165 fiat currencies, updating as you type.
- Looks up historical rates for a specific past date, back to 4 January 1999.
- Charts how a currency pair has moved over 7, 30 or 90 day ranges.
- Installs to a home screen and keeps working offline using the last known rates.

## Data source

Exchange rates are European Central Bank reference rates, retrieved through the
Frankfurter API (https://api.frankfurter.dev). The ECB publishes them once per
working day at about 16:00 CET, so every rate is dated to its publication day
rather than the moment of the request. Cryptocurrencies are not covered.
Rates are reference data for information, not dealing quotes.

## Agent interface (WebMCP)

Cambiaro registers seven tools on `document.modelContext`, each with a JSON
Schema and a typed result. An agent can discover them with `getTools()` and
invoke them with `executeTool()`; no DOM scraping is needed. Every call is
reflected in the visible UI and logged in the page's Agent Activity panel.

- `convertCurrency` — convert an amount between two currencies, optionally on a past date.
- `swapCurrencies` — swap the two currencies and reconvert.
- `setBaseCurrency` — change the currency being converted from.
- `setQuoteCurrency` — change the currency being converted to.
- `listCurrencies` — list or filter the supported currencies.
- `getHistoricalRate` — read the rate for a pair on a given day.
- `getRateTimeSeries` — read a range of rates over a date range.

Example:

    const tools = await document.modelContext.getTools()
    const convert = tools.find((t) => t.name === 'convertCurrency')
    await document.modelContext.executeTool(convert, { amount: 200, from: 'EUR', to: 'INR' })

## Answers to common questions

- Rates come from the European Central Bank, once per working day.
- History goes back to 4 January 1999 for most currencies.
- It works offline once installed, showing the last known rates with their date.
- It is free, and runs entirely client-side with no backend.
